newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Imsa says profit surges.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Imsa says profit surges.

text.p: Mexican industrial firm Grupo Imsa SA on Wednesday said its 1996 majority net profits jumped to 1.626 billion pesos ($209.5 million) versus 288 million pesos in 1995.
The group's operating income for 1996 was 1.356 billion pesos, a 91 percent increase versus the 710 million pesos reported in 1995.

"This growth, apart from the increase in revenues, is due to the efforts to improve the company's cost structure, new state of the art production lines, capacity expansion and increases in productivity," the company said.

Total sales were 8.985 billion pesos, up 12.2 percent compared to 1995 levels, it said. Domestic sales were 5.322 billion pesos, while exports fell slightly to 3.663 billion pesos from 3.936 billion in 1995.
One of Mexico's largest industrial groups, Imsa has interests in steel processing, automotive batteries and construction materials, and went public last December.

In 1996, the company's operating margin increased to 15.1 percent from 8.9 percent in 1995. "This improvement was due to better product mix and the vertical integration of the steel processing operations," the company said.
The company's integral cost of financing during the year was a gain of 203 million pesos versus a cost of 431 million pesos in 1995.
The company's current ratio was 1.50 compared to 1.02 in 1995 and its net debt to equity ratio was 0.90 at year's end versus 1.15 in 1995.
Imsa's investments in 1996 totalled 497 million pesos, focused at capacity expansion. Galvanised steel capacity increased by 70 percent and pre-painted steel production capacity by 40 percent.

"New investments in Argentina and Venezuela will increase battery production capacity from 45,000 to 150,000 batteries a month and from 60,000 to 100,000 batteries a month in each country, respectively, by the middle of 1998," it said.
